notes.made: Simon wrote the words and Michael McDonald the music. Her version was cut in New York, at Atlantic and A & R Recording between December 1977 and March 1978, with Arif Mardin producing. Richard Tee played Fender Rhodes, Steve Gadd drums, Gordon Edwards bass, Cornell Dupree and Eric Gale guitars, David Sanborn the alto solo, and James Taylor sang backing vocals.
notes.context: The Doobie Brothers recorded it first, on Livin' on the Fault Line (1977), with David Paich arranging the strings and Randy Brecker taking a trumpet solo. Simon's version led off Boys in the Trees in April 1978 and reached 6 on the Hot 100 over 18 weeks; it got a Grammy nomination for female pop vocal, and the album went Platinum. Its cover photo by Deborah Turbeville had a Danskin top airbrushed on, and the package won a Grammy.

listen_for.note: Richard Tee's Rhodes, a New York soul player's touch on an LA songwriter's chords.
David Sanborn on alto, a New York session player taking the break on a McDonald melody.
James Taylor singing harmony behind her.

leads_to.title: You Belong to Me
leads_to.why: The original on Livin' on the Fault Line, McDonald singing his own melody with a David Paich string chart.

culture.title: No. 6, 18 weeks
culture.line: Carly Simon's version reached 6 on the Hot 100 in 1978 over 18 weeks, and 4 on adult contemporary.

culture.title: Grammy nomination
culture.line: It was nominated for Best Female Pop Vocal Performance at the 1979 Grammys; Boys in the Trees won Best Album Package.

culture.title: Desperately Seeking Susan
culture.line: It's in the 1985 film Desperately Seeking Susan.

culture.title: Anita Baker
culture.line: Anita Baker recorded it in 1994 and released it in 1995 as the fourth single from Rhythm of Love.
